title: Extract intent layer for network infra and consolidate provider lockfiles
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Background:
Over time our networking Terraform templates and provider pinning strategy have diverged across repos and regions, causing frequent 'terraform plan' churn, stalled apply runs, and accidental provider upgrades in downstream workspaces. Several teams have built local workarounds (custom provider aliases, ad-hoc lifecycle blocks) which increases cognitive load and slows iteration for infra changes.

Goal:
Introduce a small abstraction — an 'intent layer' — that centralizes the representation of network change intent (subnet allocations, route table modifications, NAT lifecycle) and decouples it from workspace-level provider lockfiles. Consolidate provider lockfiles and provider-compat shims so ops / infra engineers can bump cloud provider versions once per major surface instead of per workspace. This should reduce plan noise, lower risk of accidental provider upgrades, and speed up routine network changes.

Success criteria (measurable):
- 60% reduction in workspace plan diff churn for common network changes (measured by CI plan runs)
- Time-to-apply for standard network changes reduced by 30% on average (fewer manual fixes and conflicts)
- Provider version matrix maintained in single location with documented compatibility table

Non-goals:
- This ticket will not migrate all legacy workspaces off the old VPC layouts — that will be a follow-up migration project.
- It does not change cloud account boundaries or cross-account resource ownership policies.
proposal:
High-level design:
1) Intent layer: a small set of Terraform modules (intent.*) that express high-level operations (allocate-subnet, reassign-route, nat-resize) and emit a normalized change manifest via outputs. Workspaces will consume intent.* modules rather than inlining low-level resource graphs.
2) Provider consolidation: introduce a single provider-locks repo that stores curated lockfiles and compatibility metadata for supported provider versions across regions/hardware. Each workspace will reference this repo via a submodule or remote state source during CI plan so provider constraints are consistent.
3) Compatibility shims: where API changes require adapter logic (eg. new S3/EC2 provider behavior), include lightweight wrapper modules under 'provider-shims' so migration is gradual.

Trade-offs considered:
- Centralizing lockfiles adds a cross-repo dependency and requires clear bump process. Trade-off accepted because the operational cost of decentralized locks exceeded the coordination overhead.
- Intent layer adds one extra abstraction which could be misused; mitigated via clear docs, examples, and a lint rule prohibiting inlined low-level network resources in new workspaces.
migration_steps: Create 'terraform-intent' module collection in infra-modules repo (init PR + examples)
Move provider lockfile generation into infra-provider-locks repo and publish stable v1 lockfiles
Add CI step to workspaces to fetch provider lockfiles from infra-provider-locks before plan
Pilot: migrate three low-risk dev workspaces (us-east-1, eu-west-1) to intent modules and shared locks
Iterate on shims for observed provider incompatibilities during pilot
Roll out to staging workspaces and schedule production migrations in waves
Add Terraform linter rules and pre-commit hooks to enforce intent-layer usage for new network resources
testing_plan: Create a test harness that runs 'terraform plan' across sample workspaces and compares diffs pre/post migration
End-to-end smoke: deploy and destroy a sample network change in a non-prod account and validate route/NAT behavior
CI contract tests for provider-locks publish step (verify lockfile integrity and that consumer CI can fetch and use it)
Chaos tests: simulate provider plugin version drift in a sandbox to exercise shims
Manual review of TF plan outputs by two infra engineers during pilot phase
rollout_plan: Week 1: Create module skeleton and shared provider-locks repo; announce migration plan to infra guild
Week 2-3: Pilot migrate dev workspaces; collect metrics and plan diffs; adjust module APIs
Week 4: Expand to staging and run compatibility tests; finalize docs and templates
Week 5-8: Production migrations in scheduled waves with on-call coverage; offer office hours for teams
Post-rollout: add automation for lockfile bump PRs and release notes template
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Central provider-locks becomes bottleneck for urgent provider fixes — Mitigation: on-call rotation for lockfile maintainers and fast-path patch release process
Risk: Teams resist new abstraction and continue inlining low-level resources — Mitigation: TF linter rule and CI gate preventing merges that add new low-level network resources in workspaces
Risk: Unexpected provider behavior causes failed applies — Mitigation: pilot in dev/staging, run contract tests, and provide rollback guidance (revert to previous lockfile)
Risk: Submodule or remote-lock fetching introduces CI flakiness — Mitigation: cache lockfiles in CI and add retries with fallback to last-known-good
